paragraphs: Inclusion Solutions sells universally designed access products to businesses and government agencies. The catalog runs to accessible voting booths, polling place supplies and election signage.

Its Franklin voting booth meets ADA and ADAAG standards for width, approach and clearance, and includes one lowered station. The same booth can be set up as a 2, 3 or 4 station booth depending on precinct configuration. It is one-piece construction, with legs that collapse inside the booth. For entrances that are not accessible, the company sells a push-button alert system designed for permanent installation. Its push button is described as ADA compliant and needing minimal pressure to operate. A flashing strobe provides a silent alert for people who are deaf or hard of hearing. The company also sells Pocketalk, a handheld translator it positions against Section 203 requirements. A service called the Multilingual Virtual Pollworker displays real-time information in a voter's native language.

The alert system is pitched for town halls, schools, public facilities and private businesses. The company says over 35,000 of the booths are in use in 48 states. It says Pocketalk is in use at hundreds of government offices nationwide and at election offices in multiple states. Real-time language interpretation and ADA surveying and analysis are also listed among its offerings.
